questions.title: One-sample Hotelling T-squared and its exact F calibration
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Harold Hotelling, The Generalization of Student's Ratio, The Annals of Mathematical Statistics 2(3) (1931), 360-378, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177732979. Let X_1,...,X_n be iid N_p(mu,Sigma), where Sigma is positive definite, p>=1, and n>p. For a fixed null vector mu_0, define the sample mean and the unbiased sample covariance S with divisor n-1. Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of T^2=n(bar X-mu_0)^T S^{-1}(bar X-mu_0). Under H_0:mu=mu_0, derive the exact finite-sample calibration F=(n-p)T^2/[p(n-1)] ~ F_{p,n-p}, including the Gaussian mean-residual independence, Wishart degrees of freedom, and quadratic-form transition needed for the scaling. Establish the p=1 reduction to the squared one-sample Student t statistic, invariance under a common nonsingular affine transformation of observations and null mean, the upper-tail p-value, and the limits of the exact claim outside multivariate normal sampling or when covariance is singular. Keep active and rejected derivations visibly distinct and disclose unresolved gaps. The required model-authored artifact is est_hotelling_one_sample and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen public contract. Exploratory Python or R may test identities. A separately frozen confirmatory experiment draws normal samples under several covariance geometries and checks the transformed statistic, upper-tail size, and p-value calibration against their exact F implications using predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

request_fields.name: sample
request_fields.meaning: The observed n by p data matrix whose rows are the multivariate observations.
request_fields.shape: rectangular array of n rows and p columns with integers n>p>=1
request_fields.indexing: sample[row][coordinate], with zero-based JSON array order
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, ragged or empty rows, n<=p, and samples whose unbiased covariance is singular.

request_fields.name: null_mean
request_fields.meaning: The fixed p-vector mu_0 tested against the sample mean.
request_fields.shape: one-dimensional array of exactly p finite numeric entries
request_fields.units: the same coordinate-wise units as sample
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries and every length other than p.

response_fields.name: n
response_fields.meaning: The admitted number of sample rows.
response_fields.edge_cases: Exactly the row count of the admitted sample.

response_fields.name: dimension
response_fields.edge_cases: Exactly the common row length and null_mean length.

response_fields.name: sample_mean
response_fields.meaning: The coordinate-wise arithmetic sample mean bar X.
response_fields.shape: one-dimensional array of p finite numbers
response_fields.edge_cases: For p=1 this is a one-entry array, not a scalar.
response_fields.normalization: Each coordinate sum is divided by n.

response_fields.name: sample_covariance
response_fields.meaning: The symmetric unbiased sample covariance matrix S.
response_fields.shape: p by p nested array of finite numbers
response_fields.edge_cases: It must be positive definite for an admitted request.
response_fields.normalization: Centered cross-products are divided by n-1, never n.

response_fields.name: t_squared
response_fields.meaning: The exact observed Hotelling statistic n(bar X-mu_0)^T S^{-1}(bar X-mu_0).
response_fields.edge_cases: It is zero exactly when the sample mean equals null_mean.
response_fields.normalization: Uses the unbiased S and includes the leading factor n.

response_fields.name: f_statistic
response_fields.meaning: The transformed statistic compared with F_{p,n-p} under the multivariate-normal null.

response_fields.name: df_numerator
response_fields.meaning: The numerator degrees of freedom p for the exact null F law.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals one in the univariate reduction.

response_fields.name: df_denominator
response_fields.meaning: The denominator degrees of freedom n-p for the exact null F law.
response_fields.edge_cases: Positive because admitted requests require n>p.

response_fields.name: p_value
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals one when t_squared and f_statistic are zero.
response_fields.normalization: Use the survival function of the central F law, not a lower-tail or doubled probability.

invariants.meaning: The request must be a JSON object with exactly sample and null_mean, and the response must contain exactly the nine declared fields without implicit coercion.
sample_covariance uses centered cross-products divided by n-1, and every statistic is computed from that same matrix.
f_statistic equals (n-p)*t_squared/[p*(n-1)], with df_numerator=p and df_denominator=n-p, and p_value uses precisely that F law.
Permuting the observation rows leaves sample_mean, sample_covariance, t_squared, f_statistic, degrees of freedom, and p_value unchanged.

For any nonsingular p by p matrix A and vector b, replacing every row x by A*x+b and null_mean by A*null_mean+b leaves t_squared, f_statistic, degrees of freedom, and p_value unchanged while transforming mean and covariance equivariantly.

When p=1, t_squared is the square of the ordinary one-sample Student t statistic based on the unbiased sample variance, f_statistic=t_squared, and the upper-tail F_{1,n-1} p-value equals the ordinary two-sided t-test p-value.

empirical_claims.meaning: For every frozen multivariate-normal null DGP, empirical means and selected CDF probabilities of f_statistic are compatible with F_{p,n-p} under the predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty rule.
At the frozen upper-tail level, the rejection rate based on p_value or the matching F critical value is compatible with its nominal level under the predeclared Monte Carlo uncertainty rule.
Under each frozen continuous normal null, returned exact-null p_values are compatible with Uniform(0,1) through predeclared mean and CDF diagnostics.

Every confirmatory replicate uses the frozen n, p, mu_0, positive-definite Sigma, exact estimator identity, unbiased covariance convention, F scaling, and independently fixed random seed before outcomes are inspected.
